name: Hana Reyes

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does an ordinary shift involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I answer weekend calls and chats about appliance repair bookings. I used to work at a hotel front desk, but the warranty codes still trip me up and I ask a senior agent to check unusual claims. I finished secondary school and am junior on this team, though the weekend premium lifts my pay above many agents. I have never used AI tools; I mark repair dates on a paper sheet.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58. My husband Mateo repairs furniture for local shops, and our grown son and daughter have homes of their own. We rent a small house and have eight months of expenses saved. Plenty of other contact centres are nearby, though few pay this weekend rate. I would like fewer shifts someday, but we have no settled income plan for that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the team a faster booking note is all right if the repair appointment is real. A family with a broken stove needs a person who can say who is coming.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my weekend rota would hold, and eight months saved gives Mateo and me room if a repair bill arrives. I would not treat that reserve as a reason to spend more.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep answering appliance calls and checking the repairer’s name against the booking board. In the first year I will use part of each weekend premium to pay down the small balance on our replacement water heater.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel calm about work. The customer’s stove does not get warmer because a message is tidier.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Where does your paper sheet help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If the next caller asks why nobody came, I can see the repairer’s name and the time they confirmed. The booking board and my sheet should match.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why pay the heater balance?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The heater is already installed and works. Paying the remaining bill from premiums will keep our eight months saved for a real gap.

I would check the **booking board** before promising a visit.
think: I expect my **weekend rota** and the extra premium to hold through a mild technology change.
I keep **eight months saved** for genuine income gaps.
do: Keep answering **appliance calls** and match every repairer’s name with the confirmed booking board.
Pay down the **heater balance** from weekend premiums.
feel: **Calm** about paid work and household bills.

steps.text: Keep answering weekend appliance calls and checking named repairers against booking board

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the centre should show paid weekend hours before calling an automated booking a success. A wrong visit creates another call, whether the first answer was fast or slow.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think simple bookings could move away and take my premium with them. Eight months saved gives us time, but Mateo’s furniture jobs are not always steady.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I will write down missed repair visits beside the paid weekend rota and ask my manager which shifts are staying. If the new booking screen becomes compulsory, I will learn it from a coworker on closed cases during paid hours. In the first year, if weekend hours fall, I will ask two nearby centres for advertised paid shifts and compare their full-week pay with our rent and bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the premium. I can learn a necessary button, but I do not want to practise on someone waiting for a stove repair.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could you work weekdays instead?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Possibly, if the total pay covers the house and Mateo’s repair pickups still work. I would compare the actual rota before changing centres.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you show the manager?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show the repair date, the missed visit and the next customer call. This is my own tally, not a group petition.

say: I would ask for **paid weekend hours** before praising automation.
I would count **missed repair visits** and repeat calls.
think: I expect my **weekend premium** could shrink.
I know Mateo’s **furniture work** varies, so a cut to my weekend premium would hurt us.
do: Tally **missed visits** beside the weekend rota.
Learn **required booking AI** on closed cases during paid time.
Seek **advertised paid shifts** after cuts only with rent-and-bill-covering weekly pay and workable pickups.

fieldNote: Her manager evidence is **individual**, not collective action.

steps.text: Keep tallying missed appliance visits against paid weekend hours

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the desk full thinking AI by 2028 could book repairs and answer most callers before I open my paper sheet. Hands-on robots around 2031 do not give phone work extra years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the weekend queue might close, and that would end the premium I rely on. Eight months saved is a serious cushion, but I do not want Mateo’s irregular wages carrying us alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will ask for written staffing dates and finish paying the heater bill before buying a new sofa. If my calls end in the first year after 2028, I will look for advertised paid hotel reception shifts where my old desk experience counts; I will accept only a full weekly rota whose pay covers our rent and regular bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed about losing the queue. I can search nearby hotels, but a familiar lobby is not a paid vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you need a course to go back?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would need to learn a hotel’s current booking system on the job, but I will not buy a certificate on a guess. A manager has to show an actual paid shift first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your children help with rent?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have their own households. We would tell them what changed, but I will not budget their wages as ours.

say: I would warn **2028 AGI** could book most repairs.
I would say **2031 robots** do not delay headset loss.
think: I expect the **weekend queue** might close and remove the premium that lifts my pay.
Eight months saved cannot replace **my premium** indefinitely.
do: Request **written staffing dates** and defer replacing the sofa.
Seek **advertised paid hotel shifts** only with a full rent-and-bill-covering weekly rota.
Pay down the **heater debt** from weekend wages before replacing the sofa.
S2.quote: I can search nearby hotels, but a familiar lobby is not a paid vacancy.
fieldNote: Her old hotel desk skill gives a **plausible route**, not an opening.
She assumes no **grown-child income** for rent.
She rejects paying for a **speculative certificate**.

steps.text: Keep paid appliance calls while the weekend rota remains
Seek advertised paid hotel reception shifts after closure with full weekly rent-and-bill-covering pay
Finish paying heater balance from weekend wages before replacing sofa
Delay sofa purchase until the heater balance is paid

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years lets us find actual paid work before the headset changes. General AI reaches calls in 2031; hands-on robots follow around 2034.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could return to a hotel desk if a real post opens, but I am older and would need to learn a different booking system. I would rather do that on a paid shift than promise myself a job from a vacancy page.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep my weekend calls and visit two hotels to ask what paid reception shifts are posted. If one offers a full weekly wage covering rent and bills with hours that fit Mateo’s furniture pickups, I will apply and learn its booking book from a clerk on paid time. In the first year after 2031, I will move only if those paid hours really exist.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious, though the longer window lets me look at an actual rota. Five years is not a wage, but it is time to check one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you ask the clerk?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask where the paper guest list goes when a booking changes, and who takes the late call. I would not assume my old hotel did it the same way.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no hotel hires?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will keep any paid centre shifts I can and check the other nearby centres. I will not use the eight-month reserve to pretend I have already been hired.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a decade gives us time to keep earning and compare real local shifts. Full AGI reaches calls in 2036, with hands-on robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 68 I may want less weekend work, but we have not worked out the income to replace it. Eight months saved is useful, not a date to stop working.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will keep taking weekend calls and use part of each premium to bring the reserve to ten months after the heater balance is gone. Each year I will compare actual hotel and centre rotas. In the first year after 2036, if my calls shrink, I will accept other paid hours only when the full week still covers rent and bills and fits Mateo’s pickup work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the distant change, comfortable enough with this year’s rota. I will not write a retirement day onto money that is still needed for rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you spend savings to stop weekends?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. We have no settled replacement wage, and Mateo can have slow repair months. The reserve should bridge a gap, not make one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your children join the plan?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They can visit and share a meal, but their household bills are theirs. We will plan from our own wages.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. A weekend queue could close before a hotel has paid hours to offer. A written staffing date and real advertised shifts with enough full-week pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who rings back when a repairer misses a visit twice. The customer cannot eat a promise while the stove is broken. Someone must own the second call.

headlineQuote: The customer cannot eat a promise while the stove is broken.
portrait: Hana is a **58-year-old junior agent** with secondary schooling and prior hotel reception work.
Her **weekend premium** brings higher pay despite her slow learning; she has eight months saved and many nearby jobs.
She has **never used AI**, and Mateo’s variable furniture work makes her wage important.
She checks **real hotel rotas** without presuming retirement income or grown-child support.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could close her weekend queue before a paid hotel post opens.
whatWouldHelp: A **written staffing date** and advertised shifts with rent-covering full-week pay would help.
